thread.title: Ohio House passes bill to expand parental access to children's medical records

author: C. N. Beal
title: Ohio House passes bill to expand parental access to children's medical records
text:
State Rep. Monica Robb Blasdel | The Ohio House of Representatives
State Rep. Monica Robb Blasdel | The Ohio House of Representatives
State Representative Monica Robb Blasdel (R-New Waterford) has voted in favor of House Bill 162, known as the My Child-My Chart Act. The proposed legislation aims to give parents access to their child's medical charts while ensuring compliance with existing privacy laws.
"Parents should have reasonable access to their child’s medical information while respecting existing privacy laws," said Rep. Robb Blasdel. "This bill strikes the right balance by keeping parents informed and engaged in their children’s health care."
If enacted, the bill would require health care providers using electronic health records to give parents or guardians access to their minor child's health records, as allowed under federal HIPAA rules and Ohio law.
The legislation also mandates that health care providers annually inform parents or guardians about several key points: when Ohio law allows minors to receive health care without parental consent; that records related to such care may not be disclosed to parents without the minor’s authorization; and that a minor's consent for parental access to medical records is valid only for care provided by the provider who obtained the consent.
House Bill 162 will now move to the Senate for further review.
